SUMMARY

Citigroup Inc.(C-5.60%)reported its highest third-quarter revenue in 10 years, driven by double-digit growth in its Services and Wealth segments. Management highlighted the continued execution of its transformation strategy, noting positive operating leverage and meaningful improvements in returns across four out of its five business segments. The company is prioritizing capital deployment toward high-returning client activities while maintaining a consistent pace of share repurchases. Strategic focus remains on scaling the prime services platform and integrating artificial intelligence to drive structural efficiencies and improve client engagement.

Full Conference Call Transcript

Operator:Hello, and welcome to Citi's Third Quarter 26 Earnings Call. Today's call will be hosted by Mark Mason, head of Citi's strategy, M&A, and investor relations. We ask that you please hold all questions until the completion of the formal remarks. At which time, you will be given instructions for the question and answer session. Also, as a reminder, this conference is being recorded today. If you have any objections, please disconnect at this time. Ms. Landis, you may begin.

Jennifer Landis:Thank you, operator. Good morning. And thank you all for joining our third quarter 26 earnings call. I am joined today by our Chair and Chief Executive Officer, Jane Nind Fraser. And our chief financial officer, Gonzalo Luchetti. I would like to remind you that today's presentation which is available for download on our website, citigroup.com, may contain forward looking statements which are based on management's current expectations and are subject to uncertainty and changes in circumstances. Actual results may differ materially from these statements due to a variety of factors. Including those described in our earnings materials as well as in our SEC filings. And with that, I will turn it over to Jane.

Jane Nind Fraser:Thank you, Jen, and good morning to everyone. This morning, we reported net income of $5.2 billion for the third quarter, with an EPS of $2.85 and an ROTCE of 11.5%, Our returns improved meaningfully, in services, banking, wealth and US consumer cards. The firm's ROTC grew by 180 basis points over last year, and our net income was up 17%. With revenues up 8% year over year, we delivered our best third quarter revenue in a decade. And we saw revenue growth in 4 out of our 5 businesses. As previously shared, we pulled some of our planned investments and severance into this quarter. We remain very intentional around our expenses and our investments in talent and technology.

Even with this pull forward, we delivered positive operating leverage, holding expense growth to 3% excluding last year's notable item. Our overall performance continues to demonstrate the consistent execution of our strategy. Now let's go through our 5 businesses. This was another standout quarter in services. With revenues up 15%. Growth was broad based across every driver, from deposits to commercial card spend. And we saw continued momentum in trade loans and cross border activity across the network. We continue to lead through innovation, bringing new real time capabilities to our clients, with the launch of Citi Token services in the UAE and Manan, and the introduction of Custody Plus.

Assets under custody and administration grew by 16%, and we are laser focused on winning and onboarding further new mandates. In markets, revenues were up 6%, Equities revenues were up 14% driven by our performance in prime and in Asia, where we have been investing to gain share. FICC was up 4%, Rates was pressured by the trading environment, but we saw good growth in FX and spread products. Both stable revenue streams. In banking, revenues were up 6%. We performed particularly well in ECM, where we played meaningful roles in the 6 largest transactions of the quarter. Including leading SK Hynix, the largest ever of an Asian based issuer.

And in leveraged finance, we led $11 billion high yield offering. The largest ever of its kind. I am proud of these wins and how our client relationships and bankers, including the new talent we have attracted, allowed us to land these mandates. As you have seen this quarter, we are continuing to invest responsibly in high quality talent to build on our strengths and fill identified gaps in our franchise. Wealth's performance continues to steadily improve, with growth across all 3 businesses. ROTCE was over 14%, significantly higher than last year. We brought in $38 billion in net new investment assets this quarter, up over 100% from a year ago.

We continue to launch new offerings such as Premium Boost, to deepen client relationships, and are seeing strong uptake of our wealth offering by our retail bank clients. In US consumer cards, revenues were flat as a result of higher partner payments. At the same time, our general purpose portfolio drove 6% growth in total average loans. We are increasing investment in this business, both through our deep relationships with key partners, and differentiated rewards for our customers. As you saw with the acquisition of Card. With returns of over 21% in the quarter, this is already a very attractive business, and the benefits of our investments will continue to scale over time.

In legacy franchises, we closed on the sale of a 1.4% equity stake of Banamex. Bringing the total amount divested so far to 49%. We are now busy preparing for Banamex deconsolidation from Citi next year. The IPO would happen after that, when market conditions allow, and when the usual regulatory requirements are met. At that point, our international consumer divestitures will be nearly complete. Turning to capital. We returned over $4 billion to our shareholders this quarter, including $3 billion in share buybacks. We have also utilised about £900 million of our disallowed DTA so far this year. Slightly above the path we discussed at Investor Day in May.

Our tangible book value per share rose 6% to $101.59 and our CET1 ratio stood at 12.8%, and remains about 120 basis points above our current regulatory minimum. I know that the opportunities and risks that AI presents are on everyone's mind. Our transformation has modernized our core technology platform giving us the foundation we need to implement AI firm wide. As I have said before, we are approaching AI through 4 lenses: how it can help us grow, how we can deploy it to operate more efficiently, how we can teach our people to use these new capabilities, and how we can strengthen our defences given the enhanced threat environment we and our clients face.

I have talked frequently in the past about what we are doing on the first 3, and we are excited about the top line benefits and the efficiencies we are delivering. And the many opportunities to do more for our clients. But let me spend a minute on the 4th lens. Our cyber defense strategy is about being on the front foot. About moving fast and retaining trust. We do not wait for risks to happen, we are constantly preparing and improving our defences. We are in the business of managing risk every day, and this is no different. We have been hardening our systems and running challenging and disruptive scenarios, to stress test our defenses and our responses.

We then modify our playbooks based on what we have learned, so we are ready before an event occurs, not after. We are focused on our resilience, and working with our peers and regulators on reducing systemic risk. Even as we deploy AI to improve the performance of our firm. Finally, on the macro environment, Conditions did soften a bit, during the third quarter. And while various headwinds, most recently higher energy prices and tighter monetary policies, have been challenging, the global economy has held up remarkably well, In the US, while much has been made of the AI boom, the consumer is still driving much of the growth, the labor market is stable, and companies remain active.

Our near term economic outlook remains positive. China is seeing similar benefits from AI, but without the consumer spend needed for balanced growth. And so their economy leans heavily on exports. And Europe remains structurally challenged. That backdrop is exactly why clients are leaning on our network. They are engaged and they are healthy, as you will see from our credit numbers. They are open to strategic opportunities while being keenly aware that there could be more disruptions ahead. Our focus is on delivering our network and providing the intellectual firepower to help them compete more effectively. Raise capital, or manage their supply chains. They know we will be at their side no matter what environment they face.

This quarter, was another proof point of our consistent execution and delivery in the face of a dynamic environment. In terms of the journey ahead, as know, we expect to exceed this year's ROTCE target of 10-11%, even as we pull forward the investments to support our near term target of 11-13%, But these are simply the next waypoints on our path to reach 14-15% in a sustainable manner which we will do. With that, let me turn it over to Gonzalo and then we would then both be delighted to take your questions.

Gonzalo Luchetti:Thank you, Jane and good morning, everyone. I am going to start with the firm wide financial results. Focusing on year over year comparisons unless I indicate otherwise. And then review the performance of our businesses in greater detail. On slide 4, we show financial results for the full firm. Which demonstrate the progress we have made and the momentum of our strategy. This quarter, we reported net income of $5.2 billion EPS of $2.85 an ROTCE of 11.5% on $23.8 billion of revenues, generating positive operating leverage. Total revenues were up 8% driven by growth in services, wealth, markets and banking. Partially offset by a decline in all other.

Net interest income excluding markets which you can see on the bottom left side of the slide, was up 7% driven by growth in services, wealth, and U. S. Consumer cards, partially offset by declines in Corporate/Other, and banking. Non interest revenues, excluding markets, were up 12% driven by growth in all other, services, banking, wealth, partially offset by a decline in US consumer cards. And total markets revenues were up 6%, Expenses of $14 billion were down 2% on a reported basis, with an efficiency ratio of 58.5%, Excluding the impact of the $726 million Banamex goodwill impairment notable item from the third quarter of last year, expenses were up 3%.

And cost of credit was $2.6 billion which included a firm wide net reserve build of $369 million. Looking at the firm on a year to date basis, we generated positive operating leverage and an ROTCE of 12.6%. On slide 5, we show the expense and efficiency trend over the past 5 quarters. As I just mentioned, excluding the impact of the notable item last year, expenses were up 3% primarily driven by higher transactional and product servicing, deposit insurance costs and compensation and benefits. Partially offset by lower professional services expenses.

On a year to date basis, we have recognized over $1 billion of severance, largely across functions, technology and operations as we continue to drive structural efficiencies and bring down transformation expenses and stranded costs to create capacity for business growth. On Slide 6, we show U. S. branded and corporate credit metrics. At the end of the quarter, we had over $22 billion in total reserves, with a reserve to funding loan ratio of 2.5%.

Our reserves incorporate an 8 quarter weighted average unemployment rate of 5.3%, which includes a downside scenario average unemployment rate of nearly 7%, We maintained a high quality credit card portfolio with approximately 86% of balances extended to consumers with FICO scores of 660 or higher. And a reserve to funded loan ratio in our U. S. branded portfolio of 7.7%, And we continue to see strong consumer credit performance, as both net credit loss and delinquency rates in our overall cash portfolio declined year over year.

Looking at the right hand side of the slide, you can see that our corporate exposure is 79% investment grade, and in the quarter, corporate non accrual loans as well as corporate net credit losses remained low. We are confident in the high quality nature of our portfolios, which reflect our robust risk appetite framework and rigorous client selection. Turning to capital, liquidity and the balance sheet on Slide 7. Where I will speak to sequential variances. Our total assets of $2.9 trillion increased 2%, driven by growth in trading related assets and loans. Net end of period loans increased 3% driven by growth in markets and banking.

Our $1.5 trillion deposit base remains well diversified and increased 1%, primarily driven by growth in services. We reported a 114% average LCR, and over $1 trillion of available liquidity resources. In the third quarter, we continued to deploy capital to support accretive client activity, while at the same time prioritizing the return of capital to common shareholders as evidenced by the $3 billion in buybacks and the 12% increase in our quarterly common stock dividend. We ended the quarter at a 12.8% CET1 ratio, under the binding standardized approach. Approximately 120 basis points above the 11.6% regulatory capital requirement. Turning to the businesses on slide 8, We show the results for services in the third quarter.

Revenues were up 15% driven by growth across both TTS and security services, reflecting the benefits of our continued investments in the business. NII increased 17%, driven by higher average deposit balances and deposit spreads. NIR increased 12% driven by growth in fees as we continue to see strong activity and engagement with both corporate and commercial clients. Driving momentum across underlying KPIs. Expenses increased 10%, primarily driven by higher severance as well as volume and revenue related expenses. Average loans increased 14%, largely driven by working capital loans and export agency finance. Average deposits increased 16%, primarily driven by growth in the US.

Services generated positive operating leverage, net income of $2.6 billion and an ROTCE of 31.2% in the quarter, and 29.7% year to date. Turning to markets on Slide 9, Revenues were up 6% driven by growth across both equities and fixed income. Fixed income revenues were up 4% with spread products and other fixed income up 13% driven by an increase in spread products financing revenues. And rates and currencies was flat with growth in currencies on higher volumes offset by lower revenues in rates. Equities revenues were up 14% driven by continued momentum in prime services, as balances grew by over 40%, partially offset by a decline in derivatives revenues.

Expenses increased 7%, driven by higher transactional expenses and compensation. Average loans increased 30%, primarily driven by spread products, as we executed against our Investor Day strategy to drive more stable financing revenues. Markets delivered net income of $1.7 billion and an ROTCE of 12.3% in the quarter, and 15.9% year to date. Turning to banking on slide 10, Revenues were up 6% driven by growth in investment banking and gains on loan hedges, partially offset by a decline in corporate lending. Investment banking revenues increased 9%. Driven by 77% growth in ECM, partially offset by declines of 43% in advisory and DCM, respectively.

Corporate lending revenues declined 16%, driven by lower loan spreads, partially offset by higher average loan balances and commitments. Expenses increased 8%, driven by higher compensation and continued investments in the business. Cost of credit was $23 million, consisting of $43 million in net credit losses and a net reserve release of $20 million. Banking delivered net income of $378 million and an ROTCE of 19.2% in the quarter and 17.7% year to date. Turning to wealth on slide 11, Revenues were up 15% driven by growth across all businesses. NII, which you can see on the bottom left side of the slide, increased 20% driven by higher deposit spreads and average deposit balances. Partially offset by lower mortgage spreads.

NIR was up 5%, largely driven by higher investment fee revenue. Client investment assets were up 15%, primarily driven by net new investment asset flows which were $38 billion in the quarter, contributing to over $75 billion in the last 12 months representing 11% organic growth. Expenses increased 3% driven by higher compensation. Cost of credit was $102 million, consisting of $70 million of net credit losses and a net reserve build of $32 million. Average loans were up 4%, as we continue to grow securities based lending and mortgages. Average deposits were up 3%, driven by growth in the private bank partially offset by a modest decline in Citigold and retail banking.

Wealth had a pre tax margin of 22%, generated positive operating leverage, net income of $585 million and a ROTCE of 14.3% in the quarter and 13.2% year to date. Turning to U. S. Consumer cards on slide 12. As a reminder, our year over year results continue to reflect the impact from the acquisition of the American Airlines co-branded card portfolio onboarded in April. In the quarter, revenues were flat, with growth in NII offset by a decline in NIR. NII was up 6%, driven by higher interest-earning balances. NIR was down 62%, driven by higher accruals from partner payments as well as rewards costs, reflecting our investments for growth partially offset by higher interchange and annual fees.

Consistent with the strategy we laid out at Investor Day, we saw growth in general purpose cards. With spend volume up 13% and average loans up 9%, both partially offset by declines in private label cards. Expenses increased 2%, driven by higher transactional expenses as well as advertising and marketing, as we invest to drive future acquisitions and continued customer engagement largely offset by lower compensation. Cost of credit was $1.9 billion, consisting of $1.7 billion of net credit losses and the net reserve build of $28 million primarily driven by changes in the macroeconomic outlook. US consumer cards delivered net income of $851 million and an ROTCE of 21.8% in the quarter and 21% year to date.

As I mentioned last quarter, while we expect ROTC to remain around our through the cycle target for the business, in certain quarters we do expect expense growth to outpace revenue growth as we invest in the business to drive engagement and acquisitions with some of these investments reflected as contra revenues and others as expenses. Turning to slide 13, we show results for all other on a managed basis. Which includes Corporate Other and Legacy franchises and excludes divestiture related impacts. Notably the $726 million Banamex goodwill impairment in the third quarter last year. Revenues were down 3%, driven by declines in legacy franchises and corporate other.

Expenses were down 14%, driven by lower transformation expenses in corporate other, as well as lower expenses from our exits and wind downs, which declined to a run rate of approximately $100 million in the quarter. Partially offset by the impact of Mexican peso appreciation. Cost of credit was $532 million consisting of net credit losses of $433 million driven by consumer loans in Mexico and a net reserve build of $99 million. And we have reduced the total firm wide DTAs deducted from CET1 capital by approximately $900 million year to date. As U. S. Profitability continues to improve.

Additionally, in the appendix of the presentation on slide 20, we have provided an overview of financial impacts related to the Banamex divestiture. There are 3 points that I would like to highlight: First, upon our full exit from Banamex, we expect the cumulative net capital impact to reflect The release of CET1 capital associated with the Banamex RWA removal of certain CET1 deductions, and the cumulative gains or losses over the divestiture horizon. Second, as we have shared previously, as part of the deconsolidation process, we expect to recognize an approximate $9 billion CTA related loss through the P&L in early 2027.

And third, we expect the impacts related to the deconsolidation process to be slightly accretive to our CET1 capital ratio. To close, We have included our full-year 2026 outlook on Slide 14. We expect to deliver an ROTCE above 11% for the full year, supported by NIIX markets growth in the mid- to high-6% range and continued NIR ex markets growth driven by fee momentum in services, banking, and wealth partially offset by USCC. In markets, we expect a typical seasonal decline in the fourth quarter around the same magnitude as last year, which was 20% or possibly a bit more given the strong performance so far this year.

Given this outlook for revenue, combined with our continued focus on expense discipline, we expect our full year efficiency ratio to be below 60% As it relates to credit based on the strong performance we have seen so far this year, and our expectations for the fourth quarter, we now expect a full year total U. S. Credit cards NCL rate of around 4%, the low end of the range we provided previously, while the ACL will continue to be a function of the macroeconomic environment and business volumes. And we will continue to provide the businesses with capital to pursue accretive growth opportunities, while returning capital to shareholders.

We remain confident in the strategy we laid out at Investor Day, and in our ability to deliver on all of our commitments. As we take a step back, the results in the third quarter and year to date this year represent significant progress towards our goal of improved firm wide and business performance. Our strategy is working, and we have a clear path to delivering higher, sustainable returns. With that, Jennifer and I would be glad to take your questions.

Operator:At this time, we will open the floor for questions. For today's session, we will be utilizing the raise-hand feature. If you would like to ask a question, simply click on the raise hand button at the bottom of your screen. If you have joined by phone, please press *9 to raise your hand. Once you have been called on, please unmute your audio and begin to ask your question. If you have dialed in, you can unmute by pressing *6. Please limit to 1 question. Thank you. We will now pause a moment to assemble the queue. Our first question comes from the line of John McDonald with Truist. You may now press *6.

John McDonald:Hi. Good morning. I was hoping to kick off, you could put your strong year to date results on ROTCE into context. Obviously, you have got the 12.6% ROTCE for the year and 11.5% this quarter. It implies a little bit of deceleration in the fourth quarter. You know, if you do, something ending up at 11% to 12% for the year. Understanding there is lots of factors around seasonality and how much spending you pull forward, could you speak a little bit to the near term expectations and trajectory for ROTCE for the fourth quarter? And then as you look out for the next 2 years?

Gonzalo Luchetti:Alright. Good morning, John. Thank you very much for the question. it is a great question. And I think maybe a couple of thoughts to step in there. The first is our number 1 priority is driving sustainable return improvement. that is very clear. The second piece that you can see from our results throughout this year is that our strategy is working. You are seeing the compounding effect of client intensity and execution milestone after execution milestone in a constructive backdrop but that execution is clearly there. The next piece I would mention is we have lifted our guidance now. Again from the high end of the 10-11% or a bit better than 11% to above 11.

So that hopefully gives you a sense of the confidence that we have and the discipline that we have going into the end of the year Now to your point, and I think you alluded to this on your question already, there is a natural seasonality. I just mentioned that in my remarks as it relates to markets There are other elements beyond markets too. And so when you think about the market component alone, that is about last year was about a 20% decline quarter on quarter between Q3 and Q4.

This year, as I mentioned a few minutes ago, could be a bit worse on the basis of the basis of how strong the year has been so far and kind of the dynamism in the market right now. So when you when you flow the math, similar for ROTC, even if you look historically over the last, couple of years and you adjust for the typical nodal items that may be there from time to time, you do land at a high single digits rate. And so that more or less sets you up for the above 11 that we are looking at.

But you can see kind of the confidence coming through in how we are we have been raising, the estimates over the last 30 days a couple of times over. As you look forward into 2027, I think undeniably, have business momentum. You can see that on our revenue growth, right, 7% a year ago. Ex notable items. First half of the year about 14%, this quarter about 8%, You look at the drivers, you can see the client momentum. Driving that revenue growth, so we feel very good about that. We have not moved an inch from our Investor Day commitments.

The near term targets for returns Just as a reminder for everyone, are 11% to 13% into the 2027 and 2028 time period. So we are comfortable with that. And we also tested those for a range of environments, right? So we are not expecting the sun always to be shining, the wind in our backs, and our. Us walking downhill. We have tested that for a range of outcomes. Thank you.

John McDonald:Thanks, Gonzalo. Appreciate that. And maybe just as a follow-up, a question on capital. How are you thinking about the glide path to the capital target you laid out at Investor Day? And how do rates factor into that in terms of rates and what it means for buybacks? Thank you.

Gonzalo Luchetti:Thank you for the follow-up. Maybe just to baseline everyone again, Today, we are at our CET1 of 12.8%, which is about a 120 basis points above our regulatory minimum. As per Investor Day, the regulatory minimum that we talked about and you were alluding on your question to the glide path We have talked about how we are now at 11.6% as a regulatory minimum. And we our assumption is that we go into 13.1% as a regulatory minimum starting in January 2028. At Investor Day, we gave a directional target of 13.1%. So that gives you a sense of the direction of travel We continue to be comfortable with that direction of travel.

So that I think is the key piece. The second piece is. And going into the buybacks component of your question too, I would say a couple things. First, maybe restating our framework, right? Our framework is we hold capital for resilience and flexibility. And we deploy it for returns and to distribute it to shareholders. And that is kind of the staircase that we talked about on Investor Day and that is hopefully you are seeing this apply that every single 1 of the quarters this year. Right?

When you look at this quarter, as 1 example, I feel good about how we were able to deploy our balance sheet to fuel the revenue growth that you are seeing and the improving returns year on year that you are seeing, and at the same time, billion dollars of capital to shareholders 3 of which in buybacks, while still holding an appropriate cushion above our regulatory minimum to be able to navigate the environment. So being. By the way, along the way, some OCI shifts that happened due to rates in the quarter. So I feel good about that ability to balance that equation. We did that in the preceding quarters as well.

Maybe with a bit less OCI action, but that hopefully gives you a sense of business has momentum, We do have a balanced framework in place, and we try to find the appropriate balance there always starting with, being a source of resilience. Thank you.

Operator:Thank you. For today's call, we invite a limit of 1 question plus 1 follow-up. Our next question will come from Mike Mayo with Wells Fargo. You may now unmute and ask your question.

Mike Mayo:Hey, Gonzalo. On the second quarter earnings call, you talked about pulling forward investment spending of the $5 billion over 3 years. To now, I guess, $500 million this year. How much of that has been spent in the third quarter? Why did you pull it forward? What are you spending it on? And does that mean after this year, it is $4.5 billion of investment spending, or will you increase the total? Thank you.

Gonzalo Luchetti:Alright. Yeah. Good morning, Mike. Thank you very much for the question. Maybe let me spend a second on how we think about expenses, how we think about efficiency. Again, returns number 1, sustainable return improvement but when we think about how we approach expenses, hopefully, you can see a very sharp expense discipline. that is not an initiative. that is how we operate the business every day and for every dollar. And we talked about Investor Day, that in order to unlock the client driven growth that we are aspiring to, we needed to deploy incremental investments over 3 years of about $5 billion, which we just alluded to.

And we also said that we are going to fund these investments the hard way. Via relentless structural efficiency focus. Right? We talk about stranded cost, about transformation cost, and about the structural efficiency. So that hopefully gives you a sense for how we think about expense management. So the pull forward that we talked about maybe to answer 1 piece of the question, quickly, is 100% inside the $5 billion. Right? The $500 million or so that I spoke recently about being part of that pull forward in the second half of the year. that is fully, embedded inside the $5 billion we have not moved anything related to our Investor Day, expectations.

And then to your other sub question around how much of that landed into this quarter, You can think of it as about half of it landed in this quarter. You can see about $200 million of severance in the quarter. So that is a good portion of it. And then there is a few investments extra around technology, around marketing, around client experience that we also we also support. And again, that severance is directly linked with 1 of those 3, the biggest of the 3 legs of our structure.

Of our self funding investments, which are the structural efficiency focus with the processes that Jane has alluded to in the past, the 100 plus, end to end processes that we have looked at. We review those every week. And those are part of the, unlocking through automation and AI the efficiencies that we are looking to, to deploy. Thank you.

Mike Mayo:And then 1 follow-up. Mike, you said, you are not always planning for the sun to always be shining and the wind at your back. But the return for the fourth quarter if you back into it, looks really lousy to get to 11%. When you say the sun might not always be shining, the wind's not at your back, you did say markets will not be as strong. I get it. But are you assuming something might go terribly wrong in the fourth quarter, or you just giving the usual caution and caveat?

Gonzalo Luchetti:Let me go with the latter on that. Thank you, Mike. Yeah. So we are guiding to above 11% which is again an improvement from the a bit over 11% that we talked about 30 days ago. And of course, there is a range. We could do better but it is hard to predict early in the quarter, especially how, some of the activity will play out in the market, mostly. And so it is really anchored on that. And, yes, abundance of caution. Thank you.

Operator:Our next question will come from the line of Erika Najarian with UBS.

Erika Najarian:Hi. Sorry about that delay in unmuting. Thank you for taking my question. Just to. I wanted to double click on John's question on capital. So I guess this is a bit of a compound question. For my first question, and I apologize. The way you responded to John's question is that you can continue to, deploy capital in into growth as well as keep up the space of buybacks. And I just wanted to make sure we heard that correctly because, AOCI aside, I think a lot of your investors, it is the buyback pacing is important.

And so I guess, just wanted to confirm that you can continue this pace of buyback at around these levels, even with higher rates. And, in terms of the glide path to a CET1 minimum of 13.1% by January 1, 2028. Is your understanding that Basel III endgame revisions and GSAB revisions would be mostly prospective, and you will not get any, you sort of retrospective or retroactive adjustments that could help you in terms of forward G SIB surcharge increases?

Jane Nind Fraser:Maybe if I jump in just in terms of the big picture here. You have heard us talking about a lot of upside potential. We have got a lot of different opportunities which are high returning, to be investing in. So as Gonzalo said, once we are comfortable around the resiliency of our capital base, which we feel very good about, we see a lot of opportunities to deploy capital into high returning opportunities. That will drive the growth and scale that underpins the presentation we gave at investor day and laid out that in a lot detail. We know buybacks are important. We know return of capital is important to our shareholders.

And we make that judgment as to what the right balance is. But you think all of our investors will want us to make sure that we are investing behind these long term, high return growth opportunities that will drive the performance and competitiveness of the bank. Gonzalo, over to you for the nitty gritty.

Gonzalo Luchetti:Thank you, Jane, and thank you, Erika, and good morning. Thank you for the question. So I think maybe a couple of thoughts on maybe to start on buybacks and then pull back up into the path on capital. Just as a reminder, right, what we said for this year, let me start in the year and now and then maybe without giving you the decimal precision going forward, I can describe the shape of how we think about it. In the here and now, just, completed, with this quarter of about $3 billion of repurchases. Year-to-date, $13.3 billion.

Last year was $13 billion, and we had said earlier that we expected this year to do more than last year which we just achieved in the third quarter. So we are in that sense, doing what we said we are going to do. When you think about the framework going forward, I think you highlighted, what I was talking about a little bit earlier. That we plotted at investor day. That glide path for capital for us And let me talk in maybe regulatory minimum terms.

Going from 11.6% to 12.1%. that is on the back, of course, of having enabled the business, the balance sheet, to support the high levels of activity that we have seen over the last couple of years? And have you seen us grow various businesses, not only the markets business, but also banking, and services and some of our, franchises. And so that is directly linked to that. It was expected. that is why we discussed it at Investor Day. To your point, it is a bit unknown exactly how all the rules, right, when we are done, which we should see more of those over the next, several months.

And then we will have, full visibility with models and market shock scenarios and so on. Really, we will know probably around next year the full impact that may have on glide path.
